sections.heading: Coming to you as I really am
sections.text: Great and glorious God, you are far beyond what I can understand, and still you let me come near. I worship you, and I humble myself before you. When I see myself honestly in your light, I have nothing to boast about. I am your creature, completely dependent on you, and my sin leaves me with no claim on you at all. Nothing in me is hidden from you. The thoughts I keep private, the sins I try to bury, and the motives I barely admit to myself are all open before your face.
theological_themes: human creatureliness and humility before God
God's complete knowledge of hidden sin

scripture_references.connection: This passage teaches that every creature is exposed before God and accountable to him. It grounds the prayer's honesty that secret thoughts and sins are not hidden from God's sight.
Isaiah's vision of God's holiness leads him to deep awareness of his own uncleanness. That movement matches this section's worshipful humility before the glorious God.

sections.heading: Holding on to the blood and grace of Christ
sections.text: Please keep reminding me of the blood of Jesus, strong enough to cleanse every sin. Help me believe your grace—not only as pardon for what I have done, but as power to bring my sin under your rule. I give myself to the work of your Spirit. Deliver me from the slavery of corruption and bring me into the freedom that belongs to your children.
theological_themes: grace that forgives and conquers sin
freedom as a child of God

scripture_references.connection: John connects walking in God's light with confession and cleansing through the blood of Jesus. This supports the prayer's confidence that even exposed sin can be truly cleansed.

Paul describes the Spirit putting sinful deeds to death and giving believers the status of God's children. This directly supports the prayer's request to be freed from bondage into the liberty of God's family.

sections.heading: Trusting you to finish what you started
sections.text: You have already begun your good work in me. I did not start it, and I cannot carry it to completion by my own strength. Keep working in me. Continue what you have begun, and finish it in the way only you can.
theological_themes: God's initiative in salvation and sanctification
confidence that God completes his work

scripture_references.connection: Paul expresses confidence that God will complete the good work he began in believers. This is the clearest biblical grounding for asking God to continue and finish his work in the soul.
This passage holds together real human obedience and God's deeper work within the believer. It supports the prayer's dependence on God while still seeking growth and change.

sections.heading: Asking for a softer, cleaner heart
sections.text: Give me a deeper awareness of how easily I wander and how exposed I am to sin. Do not let me become careless about my weakness. Let true faith in you purify me and soften me. Make me more compassionate, more loving, more merciful, and more considerate. Use me, even with all my weakness, as your instrument to bless other people.
theological_themes: sanctification that produces love and mercy
being useful to God for the good of others

scripture_references.connection: The psalmist asks God to search the heart and expose any grievous way. This supports the prayer's request for deeper conviction and honest self-knowledge before God.
Paul describes the fruit the Spirit produces in God's people, including love, kindness, and gentleness. This grounds the prayer's desire for a faith that becomes compassionate and tender in practice.
Believers are God's workmanship, created in Christ for good works prepared by God. This supports the request to be used as God's instrument in blessing others.

sections.heading: Wanting the real thing, not just the appearance
sections.text: Teach me to know the difference between the appearance of godliness and its real power. Keep me from having a reputation for being spiritually alive while I am dead inside. Show me the difference between self-deception and truth, between religious performance and a faith that can stand in your sight. If I am not right with you, set me right. When you set me right, keep me right. And when my life is finished, bring me home to your house in peace.
theological_themes: discernment between outward religion and true godliness
hope of final peace with God

scripture_references.connection: Paul warns about people who have the outward form of godliness while denying its power. This directly supports the prayer's concern not to settle for religious appearance without spiritual reality.
Christ confronts a church that has a name for being alive but is spiritually dead. This illuminates the prayer's plea to be truly alive before God, not merely respected as such.

Jude praises God as the one able to keep believers from falling and present them blameless before his glory. This supports the prayer's final request to be set right, kept right, and brought safely to God.
The psalm ends with confidence that God's goodness and mercy lead finally to dwelling in the house of the Lord. This supports the prayer's closing hope of coming to God's house in peace.

content_provenance.original_author: Unattributed Puritan source (compiled and edited by Arthur Bennett)
content_provenance.original_source: The Valley of Vision: A Collection of Puritan Prayers and Devotions, ed. Arthur Bennett (The Banner of Truth Trust)
content_provenance.source_copyright_status: Compilation, titles and arrangement in copyright (Banner of Truth, 1975); underlying Puritan sources are public domain.
content_provenance.modern_version_note: Contemporary prayer based on the theological themes and ideas of the historical source; not a reproduction of the original wording.

theological_issues_identified: The original's language of being 'less than nothing' and 'worse than nothing' is intentionally severe Puritan self-abasement. The adaptation preserves the theological force—no claim before God because of sin—while avoiding wording that could be heard as denying the goodness of creaturely existence or the image of God.
significant_interpretive_choices: The phrase 'that agency which can deliver me' was rendered as the work of the Holy Spirit, because the surrounding language of bondage, liberty, and sons of God closely echoes Romans 8.

The closing request to come to God's house in peace was interpreted as final perseverance and entrance into God's presence, not merely attending public worship, because it follows the lifelong request to be set right and kept right.
